questions.question: A patient with long-standing hypertension has concentric LV wall thickening. Which adaptation and mechanism best explain this?
choices: Hyperplasia from increased cardiomyocyte number
Hypertrophy from chronic pressure/afterload causing increased cardiomyocyte size
Metaplasia from replacement of cardiomyocytes
Atrophy from reduced ventricular workload
questions.explanation: Chronic pressure overload increases cardiomyocyte workload and produces hypertrophy, an increase in cell size. Persistent LVH can contribute to stiffness and diastolic dysfunction.

questions.question: Why can chronic LV hypertrophy eventually contribute to exertional dyspnea despite preserved ejection fraction?
choices: The ventricle becomes stiff, impairing relaxation and raising filling pressures
LVH always eliminates myocardial oxygen demand
Hypertrophied cells are replaced immediately by adipose tissue
The atrium no longer receives blood
questions.explanation: A hypertrophied ventricle can become stiff. Impaired relaxation raises filling pressures, which can transmit backward toward the pulmonary circulation and contribute to dyspnea.

questions.question: A patient with chronic anovulation and abnormal uterine bleeding has prolonged unopposed estrogen exposure. Which cellular process is most relevant?
choices: Endometrial hyperplasia from increased cell number
Myocardial hypertrophy from increased cell size
Skeletal-muscle atrophy from denervation
Squamous metaplasia of the airway
questions.explanation: Hyperplasia is an increase in cell number in a tissue capable of division. Persistent unopposed estrogen can drive endometrial hyperplasia and warrants cause-directed evaluation in the appropriate clinical context.

questions.question: A chronic smoker has squamous replacement of normal ciliated respiratory epithelium. Which statement is most accurate?
choices: This is metaplasia, an adaptation that can impair mucociliary clearance
This proves invasive cancer is present
This is hyperplasia because all cells enlarge
This is apoptosis because inflammation is absent
questions.explanation: Metaplasia is replacement of one mature cell type by another mature cell type better able to tolerate chronic stress. It is not cancer, but persistent injury can have important surveillance implications.

questions.question: Which mechanism most directly produces edema during acute inflammation?
choices: Decreased vascular permeability
Increased vascular permeability allowing protein-rich fluid into tissue
Reduced local blood flow from vasoconstriction
Increased plasma albumin production
questions.explanation: Inflammatory mediators increase vascular permeability. Fluid and proteins leave the vascular space, contributing to tissue edema.

questions.question: Which cellular pattern most strongly supports chronic inflammation?
choices: Predominantly neutrophils with rapid onset only
Macrophages and lymphocytes with tissue injury and repair occurring together
Erythrocytes with absent cytokine signaling
Platelets alone without tissue remodeling
questions.explanation: Chronic inflammation commonly involves macrophages and lymphocytes, persistent injury, and simultaneous repair/remodeling that may lead to fibrosis.

questions.question: A patient has fever and an elevated CRP. What is the best interpretation?
choices: These findings identify a bacterial cause without further assessment
They are inflammatory clues that must be interpreted with history, examination, severity, and a source-directed differential
They exclude tissue injury or autoimmune disease
They prove the patient requires antibiotics
questions.explanation: Fever and CRP can support an inflammatory response but do not establish its cause. Infection, sterile injury, inflammatory disease, and other conditions require clinical context.

questions.question: A patient has unilateral red, warm, swollen calf pain. Which FNP approach is safest?
choices: Diagnose cellulitis from erythema alone
Consider cellulitis, abscess, DVT, venous disease, dermatitis, and necrotizing infection; use history, exam, risk factors, and an appropriate diagnostic pathway
Assume bilateral venous stasis disease
Delay all assessment until antibiotics have failed
questions.explanation: Redness and swelling are inflammatory findings, not a diagnosis. The differential must include infection, venous disease, DVT, dermatitis, and time-sensitive alternatives when supported by the presentation.

questions.question: Which finding most strongly raises concern for necrotizing soft-tissue infection rather than uncomplicated cellulitis?
choices: Mild pruritus after a new topical product
Pain out of proportion with rapid progression and systemic toxicity
Chronic symmetric ankle discoloration
Stable erythema that improves with elevation
questions.explanation: Pain out of proportion, rapid progression, systemic toxicity, bullae, crepitus, anesthesia, and skin necrosis/discoloration are red flags. Suspected necrotizing infection needs emergency escalation.

questions.question: A patient with a rapidly progressive painful thigh infection has hypotension, bullae, and severe pain. What is the most important FNP decision?
choices: Arrange a routine office recheck after oral treatment
Wait for imaging before escalating in every case
Recognize possible necrotizing infection and arrange emergency evaluation with urgent escalation
Treat this as uncomplicated venous stasis dermatitis
questions.explanation: This is a potentially life-threatening presentation. High clinical suspicion warrants emergency evaluation and urgent escalation; imaging should not delay definitive evaluation when concern is high.
